messages.text:
Would you approve a written exception to the copying and disclosure restrictions for review and, if the film is selected, catalog preparation? We propose these terms.

- Four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer may view the unfinished cut. All five will agree in writing to keep the film confidential and use it only for the review. We can provide their names before granting access.
- Three reviewers will stream the film through individual accounts. The other two each need one offline copy on encrypted equipment. We’ll revoke access and delete both offline copies when review ends. The screener platform may retain a backup for up to 30 days after removal. Reviewers will have no access to that backup.
- A programmer may give the selection board a short oral synopsis in a closed, confidential session. The board will receive no screener, clips, or copies.
- If selected, festival staff may draft and edit the catalog entry in confidence and share it with you for factual review. We’d like permission to publish the film’s title and catalog text at the official festival announcement, even if the film’s public release comes later. Stills and clips would require separate permission.

If you need to approve the final catalog wording, we can send it before the announcement and hold publication until you clear it in writing. Can you confirm the review permissions, including offline copies and the backup, and whether factual review or final approval is your preference for the catalog?

Producer can approve the review workflow in principle, subject to the following conditions.

- **Reviewers**: Provide all five names and roles before access. Producer will approve names in writing. Each reviewer must sign a confidentiality undertaking consistent with the draft: no copying and no disclosure until public release. That undertaking must specifically prohibit describing the ending or any unannounced cast elements in any notes, discussions, or the oral synopsis.

- **Streaming/offline copies**: The three streaming accounts are acceptable only if they are individual and non-transferable, with no downloading or copying enabled. If the platform can watermark the streams, Producer requires it. The two offline copies are acceptable only on encrypted, named equipment, with individual watermarking, no further copying, and no transfer. After review, or on withdrawal, provide a deletion record identifying the person, device, date, and deletion method.

- **Platform backup**: Producer can accept the screener platform retaining a backup for up to 30 days after removal only if no reviewer or festival staff can access it and it is automatically deleted. Producer requires written confirmation of deletion after that period. If that cannot be confirmed, Producer needs a shorter backup retention period.

- **Oral synopsis**: A programmer may give the selection board a closed oral synopsis only if there is no recording, no clips or copies, and the synopsis excludes the ending and any unannounced cast elements. The board must be instructed that the information is confidential.

- **Catalog/publicity**: Producer requires final approval, not just factual review, for the title and catalog text and any publicity excerpts. You may send final text before the announcement; Producer will clear or request changes within two business days of receipt. Do not publish until Producer gives written approval. Stills and clips remain subject to separate approval.

- **Embargo and withdrawal**: The review exception does not lift the overall embargo. The only permitted publication before public release is the approved title and catalog text at the official festival announcement. Producer may withdraw the cut at any time by written notice. On withdrawal, the festival must immediately revoke all access, delete or direct deletion of offline copies and platform backups, provide deletion records within three business days, and not publish or further use the catalog text unless already published. If already published, the festival must remove the film from active promotion and confirm the removal.

Please confirm the platform and watermarking details, the deletion record format, and that the oral synopsis will exclude the protected elements. If those are confirmed, Producer can finalize the review permissions.

We accept the confidentiality and synopsis terms. Before access, we’ll submit the four programmers’ names and the outside accessibility reviewer’s name, with each person’s role and the two offline device identifiers, for your written approval. Each reviewer will sign an undertaking that incorporates the agreed review exceptions and expressly prohibits describing the ending or unannounced cast elements in notes, discussions, or the synopsis. A programmer will instruct the board to keep the information confidential and give a short oral synopsis in closed session. The synopsis will exclude both protected elements. We’ll prohibit recording and provide no clips or copies.

The platform retains a backup for 30 days after removal. We still need to confirm the platform name and its technical controls. Before access, we’ll verify that the three streaming accounts are individual and non-transferable, with downloads and copying disabled, and enable stream watermarking if available. For each offline reviewer, we’ll verify that we can supply one individually watermarked copy on the named encrypted device. The undertaking will prohibit transfer and further copying.

At review close or on written withdrawal, we’ll revoke access, remove the active screener, and direct immediate deletion of both offline copies. We’ll provide a deletion log with one entry per copy identifying the reviewer, device, deletion date and method, with the reviewer’s written confirmation. On withdrawal, we’ll send the log within three business days and identify any deletion still pending.

**Backup deletion is the open timing issue.** We’ll verify whether the backup is inaccessible to reviewers and festival staff, automatically deleted, and covered by written confirmation from the provider. On withdrawal, we propose to request immediate deletion and send you the request and its status within three business days. If the provider can delete only at scheduled expiry, may we provide its written deletion confirmation after expiry, no later than 30 days after removal for the deletion itself? If the provider cannot confirm deletion, we’ll seek a shorter, verifiable retention period and submit it for your approval before uploading the cut.

If selected, festival staff may draft the catalog entry in confidence and submit the final title and text for your written approval. We accept the two-business-day response window. Publication requires affirmative written clearance and may begin only at the official announcement. Any publicity excerpt requires your final written approval, and stills and clips require separate approval. On withdrawal, we’ll stop using unpublished text. If the entry has already appeared, we’ll remove the film from active promotion and confirm removal.

Access remains pending your approval of the names, verification of the platform and watermarking controls, and written agreement on the backup deletion timeline.

Producer accepts the review and catalog workflow on the following conditions.

- Before any upload or access, you will provide the platform name, its technical controls, and written provider confirmation that the backup is inaccessible to reviewers and festival staff and is automatically deleted no later than 30 days after removal. If the provider cannot confirm completed deletion, do not upload the cut until we approve a shorter, verifiable retention method.

- On review close or withdrawal, provide the offline deletion log within three business days. For the backup, provide within three business days after removal: the deletion request sent to the provider and its status, including the scheduled deletion date. The backup must be deleted no later than 30 days after removal. After deletion, provide the provider’s written confirmation of completed deletion within three business days.

- If the provider cannot give written confirmation of completed deletion, you must notify us immediately and use an alternative method approved in advance.

- If stream watermarking is not available on the platform, tell us before access and obtain approval for the alternative controls. Offline copies must be individually watermarked as proposed.

- Final catalog title and text remain subject to our written approval. We will respond within two business days. Publication occurs only after affirmative written clearance and only at the official announcement. If we withdraw before publication, you will not publish. If withdrawal occurs after publication, you will remove the film from active promotion and confirm removal.

Access remains conditional on our written approval of the named reviewers and devices, confirmation of the platform controls, and resolution of the backup deletion terms above.

We accept these conditions. The backup deletion terms are agreed. Upload and reviewer access remain on hold pending verification of the platform controls and your written approval of the five named reviewers and two named offline devices.

Before upload or access, we’ll provide the platform name, its streaming and watermarking controls, and the provider’s written confirmation that the backup is inaccessible to reviewers and festival staff and will be automatically deleted within 30 days of removal. We’ll verify that the provider can confirm completed deletion in writing. If it cannot, we’ll notify you immediately and use a shorter, verifiable retention method only with your advance approval. If stream watermarking is unavailable, we’ll seek your approval of alternative controls before access. Both offline copies will be individually watermarked.

At review close or on withdrawal, we’ll revoke access, remove the active screener, and direct immediate deletion of the offline copies. We’ll provide the offline deletion log within three business days of review close or withdrawal. Within three business days of screener removal, we’ll send the provider’s deletion request, its status, and the scheduled backup deletion date. We’ll send the provider’s written confirmation within three business days of completed deletion.

The agreed synopsis and catalog terms stand. If selected, we may draft the catalog entry confidentially. Publication of the title and text requires your affirmative written clearance and may occur only at the official announcement. Withdrawal before publication cancels publication. After publication, we’ll remove the film from active promotion and confirm removal.

Producer can provide a time-limited review copy with an individual soundtrack watermark, but only if the festival accepts the following access, deletion, and certification controls.

**Access copy**
- The copy will be encrypted, individually watermarked on the soundtrack, and time-limited to expire automatically on an agreed date or immediately on written withdrawal, whichever is earlier.
- Access is limited to the five named reviewers already approved or to be approved in writing.
- The festival must maintain a written access log for each opening: reviewer, date, time, device, and purpose. Producer may request the log during review and must receive the complete log at review close or withdrawal.

**Witnessed deletion**
- Each offline copy and any derivative, cache, or partial copy must be deleted in the presence of a festival-designated compliance contact and a witness acceptable to Producer.
- The deletion certificate must identify the copy, watermark ID, reviewer, device, date, time, deletion method, and confirm no residual copies remain. That signed certificate serves as the deletion record.
- On withdrawal, festival must immediately revoke access, provide the access log within 24 hours, complete witnessed deletion within 48 hours, and deliver the deletion certificate within 72 hours.

**Backup**
- Producer prefers no provider backup for this time-limited copy. If any provider backup is necessary, the previous 30-day maximum and written provider confirmation remain conditions. Producer may require a shorter period before upload.

**Catalog and publicity approval**
- Producer will clear final title and catalog text or request changes within two business days of receipt.
- If Producer is unavailable, the named alternate may approve only non-spoiler catalog copy that does not mention, hint at, or describe the ending or any unannounced cast elements. A title that does not reveal protected elements may be treated as non-spoiler.
- The named alternate cannot approve any publicity excerpt, still, clip, tagline, or text that references or risks revealing the protected elements. Those remain subject to Producer’s own written approval.
- The festival must mark each submission as “non-spoiler” or “requires Producer approval” so the alternate’s scope is clear.

**Withdrawal and compliance certification**
- Producer may withdraw by written notice at any time.
- The festival’s named compliance contact must certify in writing, within three business days of review close or withdrawal, that: all access has been revoked, all copies and backups have been deleted or scheduled for deletion as agreed, the access log is complete, and no unauthorized disclosure has occurred.
- Producer may rely on that certificate but retains a 12-month audit right to request evidence of platform backup deletion, deletion logs, or related records.

Please confirm whether the festival can support witnessed deletion and an access log, who the compliance contact and witness would be, and whether the named alternate’s limited catalog scope is acceptable.

We can support a log for every opening and witnessed deletion for both offline copies. We propose the festival’s screener administrator as compliance contact and a second festival operations staff member as witness. We’ll submit their names before access and obtain your written acceptance of the witness.

**Accessibility review.** The original watermark is incompatible with the accessibility reviewer’s offline screen reader. May we test your soundtrack watermark and expiry controls on a sample file using the same equipment? If the test succeeds, we’ll use that version in the protected screening room under a separate login restricted to the named reviewer. If the watermark still interferes, would you authorize one encrypted, time-limited copy without a watermark, solely for that reviewer on the approved device in that room? The device would stay in the room under festival control, allowing us to stop use immediately on withdrawal even while it is offline. We’ll verify the expiry and withdrawal controls before use and obtain your written approval for the configuration and expiry date. The other offline copy will carry its individual watermark.

**Records and deletion.** We’ll log the reviewer, date, time, device, and purpose of each opening, make the log available on request, and deliver it at review close or within 24 hours of withdrawal. The compliance contact and approved witness will attend deletion of each offline copy, including derivatives, caches, and partial files. Both will sign a certificate identifying the reviewer, device, copy, watermark ID, deletion date, time, and method, and confirming that no residual copies remain on the device. For any approved unwatermarked copy, we propose recording its unique copy ID. On withdrawal we’ll revoke access immediately, complete witnessed deletion within 48 hours, and deliver the signed certificates within 72 hours. At ordinary review close, we’ll deliver them within three business days.

We’ll seek direct delivery of the accessibility copy to the approved device to avoid a provider backup. If a backup is necessary, we’ll obtain your agreement on retention before upload and follow the agreed provider confirmation deadlines. We accept the three-business-day compliance certification and 12-month audit period for supporting records. We’ll identify any backup awaiting scheduled deletion in the certificate and report any compliance exception accurately.

**Press deadline.** Press copy is due one day before the ordinary review window closes. If selected, we propose sending the final title and catalog text as soon as selection is confirmed, with the exact press deadline and time zone. Can you or, if you’re unavailable, your named alternate give written clearance or request changes within one business day of receipt and by that deadline? We accept the alternate’s limited scope and will mark each submission “non-spoiler” or “requires Producer approval.” Any publicity excerpt, tagline, still, clip, or text that risks revealing protected elements goes directly to you. If the press packet needs a separate excerpt, we’ll submit its exact wording alongside the catalog text for your own expedited written approval.

Advance clearance would allow us to prepare the packet internally. External distribution stays on hold until the official announcement and affirmative written clearance. If clearance misses the press deadline, we’ll omit the film from that packet.

Producer can accept most of the proposed workflow, subject to additional safeguards for the unwatermarked accessibility copy and press clearance rules.

**Opening log and witnessed deletion**
Producer accepts the opening log and witnessed deletion procedure. Provide the screener administrator and witness names before access for written approval. The witness may not be one of the reviewers and must have no role in selecting or promoting the film beyond compliance duties.

**Accessibility review**
Producer may permit a sample-file test of the soundtrack watermark and expiry controls only if the sample contains no protected film material, audio, stills, or derivative content and is described in advance. If the test succeeds, you may use the watermarked version in the protected screening room under the named reviewer’s separate login, with downloads and copying disabled and each opening logged.

If the watermark still prevents essential screen reader access, Producer will consider one encrypted, time-limited unwatermarked copy only after receiving:

- written confirmation from the accessibility reviewer or festival technical contact that no workable watermarked alternative exists,
- the device identifier, unique copy ID, exact expiry mechanism, and room access controls,
- confirmation that the device is offline, cannot transmit or transfer files, has external ports and network functions disabled, and remains in the festival-controlled room,
- the proposed expiry date and configuration for written approval before use.

If approved, the unwatermarked copy is subject to stricter conditions:

- it may not leave the room or be accessed by anyone other than the named accessibility reviewer,
- no further copying, recording, transmission, derivative creation, or printing,
- the compliance contact or approved witness must be present for each opening, or must review and countersign the opening log within 24 hours of each access,
- on withdrawal, access must be revoked immediately, witnessed deletion completed within 48 hours, and the signed certificate delivered within 72 hours,
- the certificate must identify the unique copy ID and confirm no residual copies, caches, partial files, or derivatives remain.

This is not intended to penalize accessibility review but to offset the loss of watermark identification because the film contains protected elements.

**Records and audit**
Producer accepts the three-business-day compliance certification and 12-month retention for supporting records. Opening logs, deletion certificates, and any backup status must be available on request.

**Backup**
Direct delivery of the accessibility copy is preferred. If any platform or backup is necessary, obtain Producer’s written agreement on retention before upload and follow the previously agreed deletion confirmation deadlines.

**Press deadline**
Producer can respond to clearly marked non-spoiler title and catalog text within one business day if the exact deadline and time zone are supplied. For any publicity excerpt, tagline, still, clip, or wording that may reveal the ending or cast cameo, Producer requires separate Producer-level approval and may need up to two business days. If the deadline does not allow that, the festival must omit the film from that packet.

Producer will name an alternate only for non-spoiler catalog title/text clearance. The alternate cannot approve publicity excerpts, taglines, stills, clips, or any wording that risks revealing protected elements. If Producer or the alternate does not clear by the press deadline, omit the film from that packet.

Publication remains barred until the official announcement and affirmative written clearance. Internal packet preparation may proceed only if no external distribution occurs.

We accept the access safeguards and press clearance terms.

For the sample test, we propose a locally generated clip showing plain text and a running clock, with a spoken count recorded for the test. It will contain no material from the film. We’ll test the individual soundtrack watermark, screen reader controls, and automatic expiry on the intended device. Please confirm that we may proceed with that sample.

If the test succeeds, the named accessibility reviewer will use the watermarked copy in the protected room under a separate login, with downloads and copying disabled and each opening logged. Before film access, we’ll submit the screener administrator’s and witness’s names for written approval. The witness will have no reviewing, selection, or promotional role.

If the watermark prevents essential access, we’ll seek a separate written exception before using an unwatermarked copy. The request will include the reviewer’s or technical contact’s written finding that no workable watermarked alternative exists, the device and copy IDs, the expiry mechanism and date, and the room controls. We’ll verify that the device stays offline in the controlled room, with external ports and networking disabled and file transfer and printing blocked. Only the named reviewer may open the copy. We accept the restrictions on copying, recording, transmission, and derivatives. The compliance contact or approved witness will review and countersign each opening log entry within 24 hours.

We accept the agreed withdrawal, witnessed deletion, certification, and audit terms. For an unwatermarked copy, the signed deletion certificate will identify the unique copy ID and confirm removal of all residual files, caches, partial copies, and derivatives. We’ll use direct delivery if feasible and obtain your written agreement on retention before any platform upload.

If selected, we’ll submit the non-spoiler title and catalog text with the exact press deadline and time zone for the one-business-day response. Please identify the alternate authorized to clear that text if you’re unavailable. We’ll mark any publicity excerpt, tagline, still, clip, or potentially revealing wording “requires Producer approval” and allow up to two business days for your decision. If the required written clearance misses the deadline, we’ll omit the film from that packet. All advance preparation stays internal until the official announcement and affirmative written clearance.

Producer approves the sample test because it contains no film material. You may proceed on the intended device and report whether the individual soundtrack watermark, screen reader controls, and automatic expiry worked. The sample test does not by itself authorize film access.

The watermarked accessibility workflow is acceptable as described, including the separate login, disabled downloads and copying, opening log, and countersignature by the compliance contact or approved witness. Submit the screener administrator’s and witness’s names before film access; Producer will approve them in writing.

An unwatermarked accessibility copy is not pre-approved. Producer will consider a specific written exception only after receiving the reviewer’s or technical contact’s written finding that no workable watermarked alternative exists, the device and copy IDs, the expiry mechanism and date, and the room controls. Producer must give written approval before the unwatermarked copy is created or used. For any unwatermarked copy, use direct delivery; do not upload to a platform unless Producer agrees in advance to retention and deletion terms. The signed deletion certificate must identify the unique copy ID and confirm removal of all residual files, caches, partial copies, and derivatives.

On press clearance, Producer can accept a one-business-day response for the non-spoiler title and catalog text only if you provide the exact press deadline and time zone and submit the text early enough for a full business day. Producer will designate an alternate for that limited purpose. The title and catalog text must not disclose or imply the ending or unannounced cast elements; otherwise Producer will treat it as a revealing publicity item requiring the two-business-day approval process.

Publicity excerpts, taglines, stills, clips, and potentially revealing wording remain subject to Producer’s two-business-day written approval and will not be cleared by the alternate unless separately designated. If clearance misses the applicable deadline, omit the film from that packet.

All advance preparation remains internal and subject to withdrawal until the official announcement and affirmative written clearance.
